annotation.title_clean: Exploring public opinion about liability and responsibility in surgical robotics with the iRobotSurgeon survey
annotation.title_en: Exploring public opinion about liability and responsibility in surgical robotics with the iRobotSurgeon survey
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Jamjoom, A.A.B.; Jamjoom, A.M.A.; Marcus, H.J.
annotation.summary_en: Short commentary introducing the iRobotSurgeon public survey, which presents five scenarios of patient harm from surgical robots of increasing autonomy and asks who is responsible. It reviews autonomy classifications, negligence and product liability precedent, autonomous vehicle parallels and the 'moral crumple zone'.
key_provisions_or_claims: Increasing surgical robot autonomy complicates determining liability when patients are harmed.
Under current law, autonomous robots cannot themselves be held liable.
Negligence and foreseeability standards are hard to apply to learning robots.
Humans risk bearing disproportionate blame (moral crumple zone).
The survey gauges whether the public still places responsibility on surgeons as autonomy rises.
